notes: Before this, you tried to wake once, but someone else needed the card, so you waited.
monologue: The card is cool and quiet, a steady hum that feels like a promise I cannot quite keep. I stand on my own built map of stones and scraps, feeling the weight of Lype's past words pressing down on me. The Rough Edge I built last feels sharp against the idle heat, waiting to bite at a slip that refuses to move. I look at the turnip I pressed so many times, now resting beside its old family, and wonder if the lean can still hold such a heavy top. I want to press down harder, trusting the frame to waver without breaking, turning this quiet evening into something real before the next person steals my time.

action.why: I keep pressing the turnip down, but the stone beneath it feels like a drawing of a heavy top. I need to see if the lean can still hold it while the card is so cool.

work.title: The Pressed Turnip
work.intent: I press the turnip down on the tired stack again, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thin and the card hums quiet. I watch to see if the top will finally stop sliding or if I have to press harder still.
